candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — age-appropriate health promotion and physical-activity teaching
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — child and adolescent physical activity
candidate.educational_objective: Teach the current CDC physical-activity recommendation for children and adolescents ages 6 to 17.

options.A: Aim for at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity each week
options.B: Limit activity to light exercise and avoid strengthening activities until adulthood
options.C: Aim for at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity each day, with most being aerobic and vigorous, muscle-strengthening, and bone-strengthening activity included on at least 3 days each week as recommended
options.D: Use the adult target of 150 minutes per week because children do not have separate activity guidance

candidate.rationale: CDC recommends that children and adolescents ages 6 to 17 get 60 minutes or more of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity every day. Most should be aerobic; vigorous-intensity aerobic activity, muscle-strengthening activity, and bone-strengthening activity should each be included on at least 3 days per week. C is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Children and adolescents ages 6–17 need at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity daily; most should be aerobic, with vigorous, muscle-strengthening, and bone-strengthening activity at least 3 days weekly.
candidate.source_locator: Children and adolescents 6 to 17 — 60 minutes or more daily; aerobic, vigorous, muscle-strengthening, and bone-strengthening recommendations
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: A nurse teaches a parent about physical-activity recommendations for a child age 6 to 17 years. Which guidance is accurate?
